The senescence of the skeletal system and the reduction of bone mineral content with age are a major nutritional concern in
gerontological nutrition. In recent revisions of the recommendations, evidence for the need for increases in both vitamin D and
calcium for older persons has led to changes in the estimates of requirements for these nutrients in later life. Within the DRI system
the RDA for vitamin D for males and females over 70 years has recently been raised from 15 to 20 μg. The RDA for adults over 51–70
years is now 15 mg, as it is for young adults as well. Similar increases in vitamin D intake with age are recommended by the FAO/
